image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a chiton (marine mollusk) clinging to a dark, reddish-brown rocky substrate. The chiton has an elongated oval shape with a distinct dorsal armor consisting of eight overlapping calcareous plates embedded in a textured, leathery girdle. The plates are mottled grey and brown with visible growth lines and some darker spots. The girdle appears rough and granular. The head is not distinctly visible, consistent with the reduced head anatomy of chitons.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The anterior end of the chiton is visible and shows no protruding eyes, tentacles, or distinct head structures, matching the biological description of a reduced head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior end is blunt and indistinct.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The front edge of the animal blends smoothly into the girdle without sharp definition, appearing blunt as expected.
There are no visible antennae, eyestalks, or other sensory appendages on the dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Exactly eight distinct plate segments are visible running from anterior to posterior, overlapping correctly in a linear series.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates are clearly surrounded by a continuous, textured mantle/girdle that appears tough and leathery/granular, holding the plates in place.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The plates exhibit a natural mottled pattern of greys, browns, and creams, consistent with real chiton coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits dorsoventrally flattened profile when clinging to surfaces.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The chiton lies flat against the rock surface, showing a low-profile, flattened shape typical of adhesion.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Can curl into defensive ball when dislodged.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: This is a behavioral state not depicted in the static image; the animal is currently extended and adhered.
